question: A Codex root launched by the gate as `codex exec --json` holds its thread for the whole turn, and a root's turn can be unbounded, so the user cannot attach. Can a role instead run as a thread on the shared local app-server daemon that a later client (the user's TUI) can rejoin mid-turn?
codex_version: codex-cli 0.164.0; daemon pid 8557 `codex app-server --listen unix://` (release 0.164.0), control socket ~/.codex/app-server-control/app-server-control.sock

observed_defect.session: 01a175b2-466e-7951-812c-cdeaa4006ac8 (role b3-api-root, launched by the gate 2026-10-26T00:53Z, committed_rotation_1)
observed_defect.holder: pid 602392 `codex exec --json --model gpt-6-astra ...` (parent systemd --user), still in its first turn ~2 h after launch; last events: role_scheduler agenda, then `role_scheduler.py wait --help`
observed_defect.user_symptom: TUI resume reports the conversation is open in another app and opens read-only
observed_defect.daemon_log: 2026-10-26T02:47:42.108Z ERROR codex_core::session::session: failed to initialize thread persistence: thread-store conflict: thread 01a175b2-... already has an active writer
observed_defect.reading: the user's TUI resumes through the shared daemon; the exec process owns the thread's writer, so the daemon refuses. role_host's Codex host fact 'The process lives for one turn' is true but assumes a bounded turn; --after-adopt continue gives a root an unbounded one.

transport_facts: The control socket speaks WebSocket (HTTP 101 on upgrade); plain JSON lines through `codex app-server proxy` got no reply to initialize within 30 s.
Protocol (generate-json-schema): thread/start, turn/start, thread/resume, thread/loaded/list, thread/unsubscribe, turn/steer (requires expectedTurnId), turn/interrupt.
ThreadResumeParams doc: 'If thread_id identifies a running thread, app-server rejoins that thread.'
method: Client A: initialize, thread/start (cwd scratch, approvalPolicy never, sandbox read-only), turn/start effort low with prompt 'Run `sleep 75` exactly once, then reply done.'; A disconnects. After 5 s, client B: initialize, thread/loaded/list, thread/resume by id, reads events until turn/completed, then thread/turns/list.

result.note_on_method: A's disconnect trigger matched the word 'sleep' in the user message, so A left before the model's first output, not during the command. The entire turn therefore ran with A gone, and B received every subsequent event live.
established: A daemon-hosted turn continues after its launching client disconnects (n = 1).
A second client can thread/resume a running thread and receives its live events (n = 1).
No exec process holds the thread, so the exec writer-lock conflict does not arise for this host shape.

not_established: That the interactive TUI (`codex resume <id>` or `codex agents`) joins a daemon thread mid-turn and can type into it; needs the user at a terminal.
Behaviour with two clients attached at once (e.g. TUI plus a supervising script) and whose approvals apply.
Survival across daemon restart or `daemon update` (its help says update 'may interrupt running work').
Whether model/effort/sandbox/developer instructions set on thread/start match what the gate's `codex exec` flags set today.
Effect on role_host status/deliver/retire, which today read the exec pid and thread_history_1.sqlite.

established: turn/interrupt ends a running turn: thread status active -> idle, turn status interrupted.
A turn's shell has CODEX_THREAD_ID set to the thread id and PWD set to the thread cwd, so role_host whoami works inside daemon threads.
turn/start succeeds on a connection that never called thread/resume, and the turn completes after that connection closes.
thread/read on an unknown id fails with JSON-RPC -32600 'thread not loaded: <id>'.
Race: 20 ms after turn/start, thread/read reported idle and thread/turns/list did not yet include the new turn.
lifecycle_probe.correction: An intermediate reading during this probe took the race above for an interrupted turn 3; turn 3 had completed normally. Error class: reading state inside the visibility window. The fix in role_host counts the ledger's last turn id as running until a read shows it (test test_codex_just_started_turn_reads_as_running fails with that rule disabled).

role_host_live.sequence: launch -> running (active) -> retire without --force refused 40 -> retire --force turn_interrupted -> stopped -> deliver same thread -> running -> idle after the turn completed
